name: gh-flow
description: One-shot issue-to-PR compositions: the ordinary chain, and a relay path for a push-blocked remote.

interface.shortDescription: Carry a GitHub issue to a reviewed PR in one run
interface.longDescription: gh-flow owns the composition axis of the GitHub workflow: taking one issue all the way to a reviewed pull request in a single run, by chaining the atomic skills that live in the sibling repos. issue is the ordinary path - implement, commit, open the PR, run the review gate, then rebase-sync - and it stops dead at the first failing step with a resume hint rather than limping on. autopilot starts a step earlier, from an approved spec: it writes the plan, files the issue, implements, opens the PR, and answers review comments without asking for approval along the way, but it never merges - that stays a human decision. issue-relay and relay-merge cover the asymmetric-network case, where the destination remote accepts gh api calls but a proxy blocks git push: they probe whether a normal push actually works first, and only fall back to a per-commit patch plus gist with a git am apply-guide when a push is genuinely blocked. All four are compositions, not reimplementations - each delegates to the atomic skill that owns the step, and none of them merges a PR.
defaultPrompt: Take issue 42 from implementation all the way to a reviewed PR.
This spec is approved - run it through to a PR without checking in with me.
